title: Jesus Washes the Disciples' Feet
text:
On the evening before his arrest, Jesus was at supper with his disciples. In that time and place, guests' dusty feet were washed when they arrived, a task for the lowest servant of the house.

During the meal, Jesus got up from the table, took off his outer garment and tied a towel around his waist. He poured water into a basin and began to wash his disciples' feet and dry them with the towel.

When he came to Simon Peter, Peter protested: "Lord, are you going to wash my feet? You shall never wash my feet." Jesus answered that if he did not wash him, Peter had no part with him. Then Peter swung to the other extreme: "Lord, not my feet only, but also my hands and my head!"

When he had finished, Jesus put his garment back on, returned to his place and asked them whether they understood what he had done. "You call me Teacher and Lord, and you are right, for so I am. If I, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash one another's feet. For I have given you an example, that you should do as I have done to you."
lesson: Authority is most convincing when it is used to serve. If there is a humble task nobody wants, doing it yourself teaches your team more than any speech about values.
